title: Group By
story: The HR department hands you a flat list of employees: Alice (25), Bob (30), Carol (25), Dave (30), Eve (25). They want them grouped by age — all 25-year-olds together, all 30-year-olds together. It's time to group by!
why: Group By transforms flat lists into organized categories — the pattern behind report sections, grade groupings, tag clouds, and any system that organizes items by a shared property.
analogy: Group By is like a teacher sorting graded tests into piles — all A's together, all B's together, all C's together. The letter grade is the 'key' and each pile is a 'group Vec.' You started with a messy stack (flat Vec) and ended with organized piles (grouped Map).
try_it: Group by first letter of name: create a Map[Str, Vec[Str]] where each key is a single character and values are names starting with that letter. Then write a `group_by_grade_range` that groups scores into 'A' (90+), 'B' (80-89), etc. Print the size of each group. Bonus: sort the groups by group size to see which category is biggest.
tips: The group-by key can be anything: a field value, a computed property, a category label — the pattern is the same
When modifying a Vec inside a Map, rebuild the Vec and re-insert — don't try to modify in place
Empty groups don't appear in the Map — `groups.get(&key)` returns None for keys with no items
common_mistakes: Trying to modify a Vec retrieved from Map in-place — with move semantics, you need to rebuild and re-insert
Using the wrong key type — if grouping by age, the Map key is Int; if by name, the Map key is Str
Forgetting to push existing items into the updated Vec — only pushing the new item loses all previous data
